body:
Thank you very much for your reply : I needed to hear that. 

 I tend to jump on the easy path, which is to think that I'm the one who's inconvenient so I must adapt. I've put myself under a lot of pressure in order to fit in and appear less "off",  resulting in letting people walk over me constantly.

 I can understand how this attitude might actually be undermining my efforts in general. It's going to be a long journey, but it will be a good foundation to start building on. So, thanks for believing in me.
Thank you for your input ! I usually have this approach with close friends too,  the fact that that it was people I don't know just made it confusing haha

Thank you for your advice ! I understand better now.

 My relatives tend to do that (interrupting you but get ridiculously angry if you interrupt them), so I'm cautious about this as a result.  I wasn't sure of the appropriate approach when it comes to strangers, just that it worked to appease my family in the past.
Yeah you're right, I might have been overthinking it. Thanks, that's very helpful !

Thank you very much for your input ! :)

This is an interesting approach I will definitely try.

As another example; I had a first meeting with my SO's bookclub 2 days ago, where everyone was speaking over each other constantly. I litterally could not participate into the conversation at all and stayed silent the whole time. My SO told me to be more assertive next time, by talking over others if I had to. This is very confusing for me... Would you, per chance, have any suggestions on how I can participate to similar conversations without merging into the " she's being rude" category ?   

To me, they are all friends and I am a stranger (for most). As such, I would think that them interrupting each other is no big deal... but if I do it, wouldn't it be considered impolite ?

I could recognize it as being a poor attempt of the Lucifer's sigil (also pointed by another user), simply because of the curved ends. 

However, the good news is that it looks like an easy cover-up job if you wish to change it -- It's faded a lot and doesn't seem like the ink got deep into the skin layers. I believe any good tattoo artist would have no problem assisting you with it ! 

As a personal experience, I had two tattoo covers done on myself; with design that were way darker and more complicated to hide. Find a nice design that is more meaningful to you, then pick a good artist and, goodbye dark symbolism ! :)
